item.title: Cyclone Winds and Forest Recovery
item.description:
Twenty years of MODIS greenness data from southwest Pacific island forests show minor damage below about 50 meters per second, rising damage above that, and a sharp jump above about 75, with wide scatter.
Source article: Tropical Cyclone Impact and Forest Resilience in the Southwestern Pacific. Delaporte et al., Remote Sensing, 2022. https://doi.org/10.3390/rs14051245
This summary was generated by AI and read by a synthetic voice, for educational purposes only. It may contain errors or omissions. Consult the original article before relying on it.

item.title: Late Season Caribbean Hurricanes
item.description:
Covers the October–November 2020 Atlantic hurricane finish, with five major hurricanes driven by low wind shear and warm western Caribbean water. A simple summer model using the ENSO longitude index and Atlantic warm pool would have predicted the surge.
Source article: A Hyperactive End to the Atlantic Hurricane Season October–November 2020. Klotzbach et al., Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 2022. https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-20-0312.1

item.title: Informal Trade Behind Wiregrass Restoration
item.description:
Interviews with 20 Florida landowners, land managers, and conservation staff show wiregrass restoration runs on trust-based swaps of seed, burn crews, and equipment. Seed costs about $1,700 per pound, and goodwill, more than profit, drives the sharing.
Source article: The informal economy of wiregrass production for longleaf pine restoration in Florida. Carney et al., Trees, Forests and People, 2024. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tfp.2024.100620
